# Maven Build Lifecycle — Legacy CI Repair Workflow

## Core rule: reproduce the target CI before changing the project

For build-repair tasks, the first successful local command is not enough. The
failure must be reproduced under the toolchain and Maven command used by the
target CI. Read the repository's CI configuration (`.travis.yml`, workflow
files, wrapper scripts, build POMs) before interpreting any compiler or
dependency error.

Record at least:

```bash
java -version
javac -version
mvn -version
```

If the repository declares a historical JDK and the container's default Java
is newer, switch to the declared JDK *before* patching project files. A failure
caused only by running an old project on a modern JDK is not evidence that the
project should be migrated.

can be reproduced with:

```bash
source /opt/jdk_switcher/jdk_switcher.sh
jdk_switcher use openjdk7
export TRAVIS_JDK_VERSION=openjdk7
java -version
```

```bash
mvn -Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify \

```

# Maven Dependency Management

Master Maven dependency management including dependency declaration, scope management, version resolution, BOMs, and dependency tree optimization.

## Overview

Maven's dependency management is a cornerstone of Java project build systems. It handles transitive dependencies, version conflicts, and provides mechanisms for controlling dependency resolution across multi-module projects.

## Dependency Declaration

### Basic Dependency

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    <version>3.2.0</version>
</dependency>
```

### Dependency with Scope

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <version>5.10.1</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

### Optional Dependencies

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.code.findbugs</groupId>
    <artifactId>jsr305</artifactId>
    <version>3.0.2</version>
    <optional>true</optional>
</dependency>
```

## Dependency Scopes

### Available Scopes

| Scope | Compile CP | Test CP | Runtime CP | Transitive |
|-------|-----------|---------|------------|------------|
| compile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| provided | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| runtime | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| test | No | Yes | No | No |
| system | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| import | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |

diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The location hint points specifically to guidance in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md about handling nested/invoker-style test projects. That section likely gives incomplete or incorrect instructions about where dependency resolution failures originate and what files are allowed/appropriate to change (e.g., accidentally directing edits inside nested test projects rather than the parent reactor POM/plugin configuration that generates them). This can mislead repair behavior for builds failing around Google Auto/annotation processor dependencies in nested test modules. Other skills are generic and not implicated by the hint.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Instructions around reproducing/repairing Maven builds with nested test projects (e.g., Maven Invoker/IT projects under src/it, or plugin-generated test projects) likely mis-handle dependency resolution: it may suggest fixing by editing the nested test project's POMs directly, or it may omit the constraint that these projects are fixtures and their dependencies must usually be controlled via the parent build (plugin configuration, parent POM dependencyManagement, or the invoker test setup). This creates an overly broad/incorrect modification scope and can lead to non-deterministic or non-applicable fixes.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise the nested test project dependency-resolution section to (1) clearly distinguish fixture/nested IT project POMs from the actual build reactor, (2) instruct to first identify who owns the dependency versions (parent POM, plugin config, dependencyManagement, invoker plugin settings, prebuilt local repo, or test project templates), (3) constrain edits: prefer fixing dependency versions/scopes in the main build POM/pluginManagement and only edit nested test project POMs when they are explicit checked-in fixtures intended to be modified, and (4) add a checklist for diagnosing nested-project resolution (mvn -X, effective-pom for the IT project, verifying relativePath/parent, ensuring repositories/pluginRepositories mirror CI). Preserve unrelated guidance.
